cases.assumptions: Two-dimensional ideal-gas Euler flow with gamma=1.4 in [0,3]×[0,1] excluding the solid step x>=.6,y<.2. Uniform initial/inflow primitive state (rho,u,v,p)=(1.4,3,0,1), reflecting slip channel/step walls, right zero-gradient outflow and T=4. The reference is a separately written C++17 unsplit finite-volume implementation with primitive MUSCL generalized minmod(theta=1.5), Davis HLL flux and Heun/SSPRK2 at CFL=.3 on 240×80 and480×160 cells. Normal slopes touching walls/exterior boundaries are zero; reconstructed primitive slopes may be rescaled without altering cell means. The primary Python calculation uses piecewise-constant HLL plus Heun; flux family/time equations are shared, while implementation and spatial reconstruction are separate. No Woodward–Colella corner entropy/enthalpy reset, state floors or time-step retries are used. The uncorrected corner can produce an entropy layer that affects the downstream reflected shock/Mach stem. This is a finite-grid numerical reference, not an exact solution, rigorous error bound, replication of corner-corrected original PPM figures, or proof that fine slip lines/vortices are resolved.

cases.title: Guderley converging shock: eigenvalue and spherical semi-analytic reference
cases.assumptions: Ideal-gas Euler in spherical radial symmetry, gamma=1.4, with unshocked upstream rho0=1, u=p=0. Shells are split at the shock and conserved states are Gauss16 volume averaged, checked against Gauss32; pressure is p(Ubar). This is a dense-output adapter to ExactPack, not closed-form exact cell means or an independent similarity implementation. The figure maps 1D spherical-radial data onto a 2D meridional section, not 2D Cartesian or post-collapse evolution.
cases.reference_scope: The retained qualification actually executed pinned ExactPack eexp shooting, critical matching, eight original ramsey.state probes, shock jumps and Gauss16/32 shell checks. It freshly integrates unchanged ramsey.g, checks the new field against eight archived original-source point values, evaluates critical matching once, repeats shell quadrature and runs the separate Atlas HLL/Heun finite-volume Euler evolution. The archived point values are reused; routine replay makes no new original ramsey.state calls. Full qualification regeneration remains an explicit separate command. A dense pre-collapse adapter changes caching, evaluation and coordinates, not the ODE; this is neither an independent similarity implementation, a complete ExactPack suite nor a second numerical Euler engine.
